next_step: Confirm if procurement re-opens Q2; share throughput whitepaper + POC stress-run summary
notes:
Deal background: BridgeCrest builds low-latency ad-personalization engine (real-time auctions + multi-slot reranking). Engaged Jan 2026 after RFP for model serving. Fast initial interest: CTO + infra director wanted predictable 99th pct latency and burst headroom for auction spikes.

Timeline & activities:
- 2026-01-14: Intro call (Priya) — high level requirements: 1000 concurrent sessions, P95 < 120ms for chat/rerank paths under steady load. Mentioned strict data residency for EU clients.
- 2026-01-22: Tech deep-dive (Jordan SE) — collected sequence length distribution, 80% < 256 tokens, 10% > 1024 tokens; peak auction bursts historically ~3x baseline for 10-30s windows. Concern: queueing during bursts.
- 2026-02-03: POC kickoff — ran Redwood hosted POC with dedicated pool config (4x A100 equiv). Observations: steady-state throughput met targets, but simulated 3x burst caused queueing and 95th pct latency spikes to ~420ms; they flagged headroom insufficient. Fireflies id attached.
- 2026-02-10: Security review started; requested SOC2 + KMS integration and network diagram. Security team flagged private control plane requirement for EU data.
- 2026-02-18: Pricing discussion — BridgeCrest extremely cost-sensitive; asked for clear unit economics for burst vs reserved.
- 2026-02-24: Competitor demo reported — BridgeCrest said "Competitor can autoscale per-request without warm pools; easier capex model." Follow-up noted competitor (InferScale) promised better burst autoscaling and lower quoted price for ephemeral capacity.
- 2026-02-28: Internal change — lead ML infra PM put on hiring hold, said procurement freezing new infra spend until Q3. No active champion to push procurement.

Key technical fit / objections raised:
- Primary: throughput/capacity for short, high-amplitude bursts. POC showed queueing under 3x traffic spikes. Team worried about missed auctions and revenue impact.
- Secondary: concerns about cost of maintaining warm capacity vs competitor's serverless claim.
- Security: must support VPC/private control plane + KMS and provide EU data residency proof.

What Redwood proposed:
- Dedicated pool + burst capacity plan: can add burst nodes and configure autoscaling policy with warm standby. Proposed stress test run with larger pool sizing and KV cache tuning. Shared throughput whitepaper and cost model.
- Private deployment option to satisfy security + residency.
- Optimize recommendations: quantization profile to reduce GPU memory, adaptive batching to preserve latency under spikes.

Why stalled / current state:
- Procurement freeze and no internal champion after infra PM reassignment.
- BridgeCrest received a lower-price, autoscaling-focused pitch from InferScale; they verbally moved forward with competitor for initial pilots.
- Security review still open; legal requires more detailed control-plane docs (we provided but follow-up stalled).

Next steps attempted / recommended:
- Short term: offer a paid short stress-test run with agreed SLAs to demonstrate burst headroom (customer receptive but procurement blocked).
- Medium term: re-engage in Q2 when budget re-opens; supply tailored cost comparison vs InferScale and updated stress-test results.
- Outreach: Priya to reconnect with CTO and infra director mid-May, Jordan to prepare scaled-run test plan.

Sales notes / playbook snippets:
- Champion risk: no internal sponsor; pursue exec-level touch (CTO) not just infra PM.
- Technical counter to competitor: emphasize predictable tail latency (SLOs) and observability (token-level cost, per-route dashboards) vs opaque serverless claims.
- Pricing play: structure hybrid reserved + burst credit package to limit baseline cost while providing guaranteed burst headroom.

Recent status summary: Stalled (evaluation). Customer effectively moved budget to competitor pilot and procurement freeze prevents new commitment. Re-open if procurement unfreezes or competitor fails to deliver on burst SLAs.
